facts.fact: Access Now says Angola shut down the internet for the first time in July 2025, for at least three hours, in response to planned anti-government protests against rising fuel prices.
Access Now lists the Central African Republic among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now lists Cameroon among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now says the Democratic Republic of the Congo shut down the internet across Goma throughout a humanitarian crisis in 2025.
Access Now lists Ethiopia among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now lists Guinea among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now lists Guinea-Bissau among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now says the Government of Equatorial Guinea continued to effectively cut the island of Annobon off from the rest of the world in 2025.
Access Now lists Kenya among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now lists Nigeria among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now lists South Sudan among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now lists Chad among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now lists Togo among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.
Access Now says Tanzania shut down the internet eight times in 2025, including twice during the election period.
Access Now says Uganda continued to block Facebook for the fifth year running in 2025.
